comments.author: TimeBearingDown
comments.story_title: Ubuntu 24.04 (and Debian) removed libsystemd from SSH server dependencies
comments.why_zh: 对 systemd 技术优点的出色而有趣的讨论。
comments.quote_zh: 对 systemd 的技术优点有一段出色又有趣的讨论。
comments.text_zh: 你这么说很有意思？这和我从 Arch 以前使用的“BSD 风格”rc.d init 迁移到 systemd 的经历完全相反。有什么具体问题吗？我没看到任何问题。无意冒犯。一个因素可能是 Arch 优先不打上游补丁——这帮助它们免于在这方面成为目标，而且它在默认配置上不会做得太过火，这一点我长期以来很欣赏。不想引发发行版战争，我非常感激 Debian。我的背景是 00 年代中期接触 Linux，弄坏了许多 SuSE、Ubuntu 以及一两个 Debian 系统，直到 2008 年在 Arch 上找到了我能理解、修复和维护的东西。systemd 突出了它与企业 Linux 保持相关性的能力，使打包变得更容易，对我来说也是诊断服务问题和管理不良软件的有用工具。我不确定它在这里被发过多少次，但前 FreeBSD Core Team 成员 Benno Rice 对 systemd 的技术优点有一段出色又有趣的讨论。[VIDEO]
comments.text: It’s interesting you say that? It runs completely counter to my experience coming from the “BSD-style” rc.d init Arch used to use, and migrating to systemd. Any specific issues? I didn’t see any. No offense. One factor may be that Arch prioritizes not patching upstream - helped save them from targeting here, and it doesn’t go overboard with default configs, which I’ve long appreciated. Not to distro-war, I’m very grateful for Debian. My background is finding Linux in the mid-00s and breaking many SuSE, Ubuntu, and one or two Debian systems before finding something I could understand, repair, and maintain in 2008 Arch. systemd accentuated its ability to stay relevant with enterprise Linux, made it even easier to package for, and has been a useful tool in diagnosing service issues and managing bad software for me. I’m not sure how often it’s posted here but Benno Rice formerly of FreeBSD Core Team has an excellent and amusing discussion of systemd’s technical merits. [VIDEO]

comments.author: eropple
comments.story_title: A BSD person tries Alpine Linux
comments.why_zh: 以 BSD 为根基、对 systemd 优缺点的公允看法。

comments.text_zh: > 通过复制 svchost.exe 把 Linux 变成 Windows，不应该受到 Linux 社区的称赞。…… 我们让 Linux 的 PID 1（对大多数发行版而言）由一名微软员工控制，而他却复制了 Windows 的 svchost.exe。大家还都很兴奋？systemd 是相当有意识地照着 launchd 设计的，而不是 svchost。目标——而且理由充分——是让 Linux 表现得像一个已经存在的、更一体化的类 Unix 系统：MacOS。Benno Rice 有一个关于 systemd 的精彩演讲，值得看到最后；与大多数拍桌子式的论调不同（“它不过是 svchost.exe！！”正是这种论调），他提供了一个我认为相当公允——而且对我来说有趣的是，一个根植于 BSD 的——视角，来看 systemd 强在哪里、弱在哪里。[VIDEO]
comments.text: > Turning Linux into Windows by replicating svchost.exe shouldn't be applauded by the Linux community. ... We've got Linux's PID 1 (for most distros) controlled by a MS employee, who replicated Windows' svchost.exe. And people are all excited? systemd was pretty consciously patterned after launchd, not svchost. The goal was, and for good reasons, to make Linux behave like a more integrated Unix-like that already existed: MacOS. Benno Rice has an excellent presentation on systemd that's worth watching through to the end; unlike most of the table-pounding (and "it's just svchost.exe!!" is exactly that), he provides what I think is a pretty fair--and, interestingly to me, a BSD-grounded--view as to where systemd is strong and is weak. [VIDEO]

comments.text: I think that the section on change at is great. The first 1500 seconds are about systemd any why it is and what it's trying to do, but that doesn't really get to the core of why I complain about it. [VIDEO] Systemd is change. Massive change that's being forced on us by a twat. Unlike Linux, which was a kernel delivered by a twat but was take-it or leave-it, this is being forced on us. It's untrustworthy and threatening and unknown. In some cases it's an attack on our identity -- "the way you did it in the past is rubbish, do it this way". Clearly we are going to be defensive about it. This isn't unique to people who've used linux for the last 3 decades. Douglas Adams knew this 20 years ago: 1) everything that’s already in the world when you’re born is just normal; 2) anything that gets invented between then and before you turn thirty is incredibly exciting and creative and with any luck you can make a career out of it; 3) anything that gets invented after you’re thirty is against the natural order of things and the beginning of the end of civilization as we know it until it’s been around for about ten years when it gradually turns out to be alright really.” His original article (in a newspaper - remember them?) is at [LINK] He mentions John Humphrys and his sneering view of this new fangled internet. comments.author: znpy
comments.story_title: Ask HN: What stops you from using BSD as main workstation OS?
comments.why_zh: 为什么 BSD 缺少像 systemd 那样的系统管理层。
comments.quote_zh: BSD 完全没有这些东西——见
comments.text_zh:
- 开箱即用的硬件支持：我可以拿到一台工作笔记本，装上 Debian 或衍生版再加 XFCE，我就知道大多数硬件都能开箱即用，不用太折腾（包括但不限于：摄像头、显卡、无线/蓝牙、Thunderbolt 扩展坞）。
- 容器：它们就是非常好用。FreeBSD 看起来具备让容器跑起来的大部分部件，但这不是他们的优先事项。Joyend 的人做了这件事，重新实现 docker server API 来管理底层 zones。我纳闷为什么 FreeBSD 不做类似的事情。
- 参考文档：我尽量使用 RHEL 及衍生版（CentOS），它的参考文档真是、真是、真是好，详尽又完整。FreeBSD 参考指南不错，但不如 RHEL 文档那么全面和/或及时更新。
- systemd 和 NetworkManager：它们非常可靠、久经考验、设计周到。systemd 远不止是 init，还做了大量系统管理工作，这些工作以前根本没有别的东西在做。BSD 完全缺少这些——见 [VIDEO]
comments.text: - Hardware support out of the box I can be given a work laptop, slap some Debian or derivative along with XFCE, and I know that most hardware will work out of the box without much fuss (including but not limited to: webcams, video cards, wireless/bluetooth, thunderbolt docking station). - Containers They're just very good. FreeBSD looks like it has most of the pieces to get containers going but it's not their priority to get that going. The people at Joyend did that, reimplementing the docker server APIs to manage underlying zones. I wonder why don't FreeBSD do something similar. - Reference documentation I like to use RHEL and derivatives (CentOS) when I can, and the reference documentation its so, so, so good , ample and complete. The FreeBSD reference guide is good, but not as thorough and/or up to date as the RHEL documentation. - systemd & NetworkManager They're rock solid, battle tested and well-thought. systemd is much more than init and does a lot of system management, stuff that previously was simply not being done by anything else. BSDs lack that completely -- see [VIDEO]

comments.author: Levitating
comments.story_title: PipeWire 1.0.0
comments.why_zh: Benno Rice 关于内核与用户空间之间存在一个 system 层的想法。
comments.quote_zh: 我喜欢 Benno Rice 所说的[1]，关于除内核和用户空间之外的第三个“system”层。
comments.text_zh: 我喜欢 Benno Rice 所说的[1]，关于除内核和用户空间之外的第三个“system”层。systemd 试图通过提供一整套彼此集成良好的工具来完全填补这个空间。但你并非被迫使用所有这些工具，你并非被迫用 resolved 取代 resolvconf。> 它应该只把一件事做好。我知道这是一个流行的原则，有些人认为它是 unix 哲学的一部分。但操作系统也应当保持一致性。有些工具可以自行其是，独立于系统其余部分。但我认为这最适合简单的用户空间工具，而不是紧密集成的系统服务。无论如何，我真的很喜欢 resolved。[1]: [VIDEO]
comments.text: I like what Benno Rice said[1] concerning a third "system" layer other than kernel and userspace. Systemd tries to fill that space entirely by providing a suite of tools that integrate well with another. But you are not forced to use these all of these, you're not forced to use resolved over resolvconf. > It should only do one thing well. I know this is a popular principle that some believe to be part of the unix philosophy. But an OS should also be coherent. Some tools can do their own thing and be independent from the rest of the system. But I think this works best for simple userland tools, not tightly integrated system services. In any case I really like resolved. [1]: [VIDEO]
